clue.text: A fighting man holds with fruit being provided

indicators.note: the fighting man is said to hold the next word, so it goes inside him

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with a navy
'and' means together with

explanation.surface: A soldier carries fruit as part of his supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link here but the word it means; 'being provided' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarine is a small citrus, a variant spelling of the mandarin orange.

clue.text: To strike in a recession would be beastly!

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so these letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hitting someone during an economic slump would be a beastly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks like economics; in this down light it signals reading the strike-in-a run upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly in the sense of belonging to a creature of the wild rather than a person.

clue.text: Detail changes and blow up!

indicators.note: the word detail changes its letter order here

explanation.surface: A detail is altered and a row erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up something such as a balloon or a pupil is to widen or swell it.

clue.text: Soldiers draw back pay

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: back says the word for draw is set down reversed

parts.note: a draw read backwards is a ward

explanation.surface: Soldiers are drawing their back pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back pay' reads as one phrase, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay and 'pay' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something paid or given in return for service.

clue.text: Hector in time may well become this shape

indicators.note: the word for hector sits in the word for time

parts.note: noon is a time of day, midday
to hector is to bully or nag

explanation.surface: A bully, given time, might turn into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' with a capital looks like the Trojan hero; it is the verb to hector, to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a geometrical figure with nine sides.

clue.text: Prepared to create a scene

parts.note: reads as being ready to make a fuss, but describes actors practising a scene before a performance

explanation.surface: Someone is all set to make a fuss in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who have practised a play or scene beforehand have gone over it so they are ready.

clue.text: A woman will fill cracked food-containers naturally

indicators.note: the woman's words fill, sitting inside, the word for cracked

parts.note: cracked means mad, nuts
she'll is the short form of she will

explanation.surface: A woman will refill broken food tins.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: nature packages its kernels in these hard cases.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard casing round a kernel is nature's own package for the food inside.

clue.text: His Eminence, uncultured and really not caring

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Eminence, a cardinal's title
artless can mean lacking art or culture

explanation.surface: A cardinal is described as boorish and quite uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartless means callous, lacking all sympathy for others.

clue.text: About to amalgamate in decline

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
to fuse is to blend or merge

explanation.surface: A merger is on the point of happening during a downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse is to turn down an offer.

clue.text: Waving an account due for payment?

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
owing means still to be paid

explanation.surface: Someone flaps an unpaid invoice about.
explanation.definitionFit: Billowing describes something swelling and rippling like a flag or sail in the wind.

clue.text: Look sly about the craft that's not so great

indicators.note: the word for a sly look goes about, around, the craft

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lecherously
SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A shifty glance at a boat that is not much to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests cunning beside 'sly', but it means a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser means smaller or of lower importance.

clue.text: Sugar and peat may be mixed into cattle-feed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are mixed together, a rearranging signal

explanation.surface: A farmer blends sugar and peat to make fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be mixed' rearranges SUGAR and PEAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grazing land or the grass cattle eat from it.

clue.text: The author of Golden Spring

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Names the writer of a book called Golden Spring.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldry term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the English novelist who wrote 1984 and Animal Farm.

clue.text: Carol's after a soft vegetable that's satisfying

indicators.note: the carol word comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a pea is a vegetable
carol is to sing; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A carol follows a mushy vegetable that fills you up.
explanation.walkthrough: P for soft comes from musical notation, where p marks a quiet passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeasing means pacifying or contenting someone by meeting their demands.

clue.text: Get in — it's a bad move

indicators.note: bad hints the letters are in a wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that getting in is an unwise move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges GETIN and ITSA.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate is to set something in motion, as one might move to start a process.

clue.text: The leading man

parts.note: reads as the star of a film, but means the head male of a family or tribe

explanation.surface: Picks out the star of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family, clan or church.

clue.text: A single ball-bearing

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of O
NE, northeast, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A lone steel ball from a bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball-bearing' splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the number of a single item.

clue.text: In control -definitely mature

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Being in charge is definitely a sign of being grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across contrOL Definitely.
explanation.definitionFit: Old means advanced in years, grown up.

clue.text: Close finish

definitions.meaning: a close is the conclusion of something
a finish is the final part

explanation.definitionFit: End is the last part, the conclusion or the stopping point of something.

clue.text: Establishing lead all round in a game

indicators.note: the lead and all go round the word in

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game is being set up with lead all around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Establishing' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinball is an arcade game played on a sloping table with flippers.

clue.text: Jabbers and so provokes 31

definitions.meaning: things that jab, sharp pointed spikes
provokes by teasing someone, the answer at 31 across

explanation.definitionFit: Needles are pointed tools that prick, and to needle someone is to annoy them with taunts.

clue.text: Churchman occupied by a father

indicators.note: the churchman is occupied by, holds inside, the letter

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a churchman

explanation.surface: A clergyman is taken up by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by' puts A inside DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad is a familiar word for a male parent.

clue.text: Giving people a rise, one makes a bloomer!

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Lifting people's spirits, someone makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns MEN into NEM, read upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemone is a flower, and a bloomer is something that blooms.

clue.text: Complete set of books written in the country

indicators.note: the books are written inside the name of the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of books written in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' in crosswords often means the New or Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: An acid test

parts.note: reads as the idiom for a decisive trial, but literally is a chemical check for acidity

explanation.surface: Describes a decisive trial of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus is a dye that turns red in acid, used as a chemical indicator.

clue.text: Gain support from the French (unnamed)

parts.note: le is French for the
anon, short for anonymous, means unnamed

explanation.surface: Getting help from an anonymous French source.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is to rely on them for help.

clue.text: Instruct as a group in the main

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea; a group of fish there is a shoal

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to train, and a school is a shoal of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Anything but a telling propensity

parts.note: a tendency that is the opposite of telling, that is, of keeping quiet

explanation.surface: Describes a character that is far from forthcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is reluctance to speak or reveal one's thoughts.

clue.text: Indicate a sling should be used

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice that a sling ought to be worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be used' rearranges ASLING.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal is to show or point out by a sign or gesture.

clue.text: Hill the instructor is such a bully!

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
a mentor is a teacher or guide

explanation.surface: Someone named Hill is a teacher who intimidates pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' with a capital reads as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is one who persecutes or harasses others.

clue.text: Once it appears make observations

indicators.note: the two words appear again in a different form, a weak rearrangement signal

explanation.surface: As soon as something shows up, comments are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' rearranges ONCEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or remark upon something.

clue.text: With a certain imitation drink alone

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one by one, alone

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a fake brew by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasingly means in a mocking way, as when mimicking someone to tease them.
